The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\frac{x}{2}\le y\le \frac{1}{2}\}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x)$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=\frac{x}{2}\,⟹\,x=2y.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le \frac{1}{2},\,0\le x\le 2y\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/09f6f71eaf66fe10e73b80ae59a30ddd04478de71dbe37c749674ac9f10d5bd4.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x/2}^{1/2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}{\int }_{0}^{2y}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})[{\int }_{0}^{2y}\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})[x]_{0}^{2y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}2y\,\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2})]_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{1}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$
